transcript.text: induction hob keeps turnin off after 5-10 mins on high, have to keep restartin it. drives me nuts. any1 know y?

That sounds like the safety thermostat kicking in because the hob is getting too hot. On induction hobs, this usually happens for one of two reasons: either the internal cooling fan isn't working (or its vents are blocked), or a specific zone has overheated due to the pan used. To narrow it down, please check these two things:
1. When you turn the hob on high, can you hear/feel a fan running inside? If yes, is air blowing out of any vents at the front or sides?
2. Does an error code (like 'E' followed by numbers) appear on the display when it cuts out? If there's no fan noise and vents are blocked, that points to a cooling fault. If there is a code, tell me exactly what it says.
yeah fan roars loudly before it cuts out. a small code flashes sometimes but didnt catch what it says. started after new drawer unit fitted under it a month ago

The fact that the fan is roaring loudly right before it cuts out suggests the system is working hard to cool down but hitting a thermal limit. Since this started after the new drawer was fitted, the most likely cause is restricted airflow. Induction hobs need space underneath for air to circulate and carry heat away from the electronics. If the new unit is too close or blocking the intake vents, the hob will overheat quickly on high power and shut down as a safety measure, even if the fan itself is fine. Please check:
1. Is there at least 2-3cm of clear space between the bottom of the hob and the top of the drawer unit?
2. Are any cables or packaging materials blocking the vents underneath? If the clearance is tight or blocked, try using a zone on high for 10 minutes with that gap open to see if it stays on. If it does, you'll need to adjust the installation to ensure proper airflow.
not pulling the drawer out or lookin under the hob, not doin that. is there anythin else it could be?

We have to work with what we can see and do. The roaring fan suggests the hob is trying desperately to cool down but hitting a limit. Because this started after the drawer was fitted, restricted airflow is still the top suspect—even if the fan itself is fine, it can't pull enough air if the vents are blocked or the gap is too tight. The other possibility is that a temperature sensor inside has failed or drifted, telling the board it's hot when it isn't. This is less likely given the timing with the drawer installation, but possible. 1. Look at the side of the hob where it meets the new drawer unit. Is there a visible gap? If you can see at least 2-3cm of space between the bottom edge of the hob and the top of the drawer, airflow is likely adequate from that angle.
2. Try using only ONE zone on high for 10 minutes (don't use multiple zones). If it stays on this time, it suggests the heat load was too high for the restricted space. If it cuts out again even with just one zone and a visible gap, it points more towards an internal sensor or board fault. Let me know what you see regarding the gap and whether single-zone use makes a difference.
cant tell on the gap, not lookin under there. it mostly cuts out on the big front zone on high anyway, usually just 1 pan on. so what else could it be?

Since the fan is roaring and it cuts out after 5-10 minutes on high power, the hob's safety system is detecting excessive heat. The most likely cause remains restricted airflow from that new drawer unit blocking the intake vents underneath. Even if the fan works, it can't cool the electronics fast enough if air can't get in. The other possibility is a faulty internal temperature sensor or control board, but given the timing with the drawer installation, airflow is still the primary suspect. To help narrow this down further while you wait to check the gap later: what kind of pan are you using on that big front zone? Induction hobs work best with heavy, flat-bottomed pans (like cast iron or thick stainless steel). If you're using a thinner aluminium or copper pan (even if it has a magnetic base), it can cause the zone to run hotter than normal and trigger the safety cut-out sooner. Try a different, heavier pan on that zone next time and see if it stays on longer.
just normal induction pans, magnetic and flat. its only done this since the drawer went in tho. so is it the drawer or not?

It is probably the drawer. Here is why: 1. The timing matches exactly (started a month ago when the drawer was fitted).
2. The fan is roaring loudly right before it cuts out. This means the hob knows it is getting too hot and is trying its hardest to cool down, but it cannot get enough air in because the new unit is blocking the vents underneath.
3. It happens on high power, which generates the most heat. Since you are not going to look under there or pull the drawer out, we have to accept that the airflow is likely blocked. The hob is doing exactly what it should do: shutting itself off to stop from being damaged by overheating. What you can do now:
• Try using only one zone at a time (you are already doing this).
• Avoid using the 'boost' or 'power max' functions if your hob has them, as these generate more heat than standard high settings.
• If it still cuts out after 5 minutes on just one zone, you will need to call an engineer. They can check if a sensor is faulty, but given the timing with the drawer, they will likely tell you that the installation needs adjusting to allow airflow. For now, keep using lower settings or single zones and see if it lasts longer.

candidates: Overheating protection triggered (cooling fan blocked/failed or vents obstructed) (high)
Power module overheating due to incorrect cookware or excessive load (medium)
